verdict.rationale: Navan's own pricing page lists 'Unlimited policy and approval workflows', and its MCP docs describe transactions being flagged against policy and routed to approvers. That is a narrow, product-native form of rules that trigger actions (flag, route for approval) when an expense event occurs. The webhooks mention is only a developer building block and earns no credit. missing for 10: documented general-purpose rule/trigger builder, configurable event types and action catalog, detail on how rules are defined, AI-native authoring of automations, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: understand why a transaction was flagged, who needs to approve it, and what policy applies.
